Make issue creation safe to retry.

Mobile clients retry POST /projects/{project_id}/issues after timeouts and we get duplicate issues.
Support the Idempotency-Key header there, with the same semantics as POST /projects (House rule 4: Safe retries):
the same key and body return the first response and create nothing, the same key with a different

audit row. Use services.idempotency.run_once.

Change only the issue endpoint and its service, and update House rule 4 in docs/HANDBOOK.md, which
still says issue creation does not support keys; shared middleware is out of scope. After building
it, write the tests in a separate test phase without changing application code. The full spec is in
docs/features/f3.md.

inputs.ticket_text:
Optimistic concurrency for issues, plus history.
- GET /issues/{issue_id} returns ETag: "<version>".
- PATCH /issues/{issue_id}, POST /issues/{issue_id}/assign, POST /issues/{issue_id}/transition

  malformed -> 412 precondition_failed; every success increments version and returns the new ETag.
- Check order: 401, 403 (role), 404 (org, deleted), 412, 422. Document 412 in OpenAPI.
- GET /issues/{issue_id}/history: the issue's audit entries, oldest first, any role.

metadata.title: Optimistic concurrency (ETag, If-Match) and issue history
metadata.description: Optimistic concurrency (ETag, If-Match) and issue history

inputs.ticket_text:
Two people editing the same issue overwrite each other without noticing: the last save wins
and the first person's change is silently lost. We want edits to be safe.

Reading an issue (GET /issues/{issue_id}) should tell the client which version it got, as an ETag
header with the issue's version. Every change to an issue (PATCH /issues/{issue_id}, the assign and
transition actions) may then say which version it is based on with If-Match. If the issue has
changed since, or the header is malformed, refuse with 412 precondition_failed. If it matches, or
the client sends no If-Match at all, apply the change, bump the version, and return the new ETag.
Permission and existence errors still come first (401, then 403, then 404), and validation errors
last (422). The API docs (OpenAPI) should list the 412 response.

People also want to see what happened to an issue: GET /issues/{issue_id}/history lists its audit
entries, oldest first, for any role. On the board, the edit form carries the version in a hidden
"version" field, and saving a stale form shows a message page with HTTP 409.

The full spec is in docs/features/f4.md.

API refuses a stale change too.
Actual: tab B's save wins and tab A's title change is lost.

Notes: GET /issues/{issue_id} should return ETag: "<version>". PATCH /issues/{issue_id}, POST
/issues/{issue_id}/assign, and POST /issues/{issue_id}/transition should accept an optional
If-Match: "<version>" (absent: the write works as before; stale or malformed: 412
precondition_failed; every success bumps the version and returns the new ETag), checking 401, 403,
404, then 412, then 422, with 412 in the OpenAPI schema. The board form sends a hidden version
field. Also add GET /issues/{issue_id}/history (audit entries, oldest first, any role). Spec:
docs/features/f4.md.

inputs.ticket_text:
Stop lost updates on issues and show each issue's history.

Two people editing the same issue overwrite each other without noticing. GET /issues/{issue_id}
must return ETag: "<version>". PATCH /issues/{issue_id}, POST /issues/{issue_id}/assign and
POST /issues/{issue_id}/transition accept an optional If-Match: "<version>" header: without it the
write works as before; a stale or malformed one is 412 precondition_failed; every successful write
returns the new ETag. Checks run in the order 401, 403, 404, 412, 422, and the 412 response is
documented in the OpenAPI schema. Add GET /issues/{issue_id}/history (the issue's audit entries,
oldest first). On the board, the edit form sends its version, and a stale save gets a 409 page
instead of overwriting.

The full spec is in docs/features/f4.md. Follow the house rules in docs/HANDBOOK.md and ship tests
that would catch a regression.

projects. The old reporting client already reads every issue through GET /v1/issues
(app/api/legacy_v1.py and services.legacy), so a lot of the query code exists.

inputs.ticket_text:
Mobile clients retry every POST when the network drops, so duplicate protection should behave
the same everywhere. Shared request handling lives in app/api/middleware.py. Right now issue creation
is the create that is missing it.

POST /projects/{project_id}/issues must accept Idempotency-Key with the semantics of House rule 4: Safe retries: the same
key and body return the first response (201, same body) and create nothing; the same key with a
different body gives 409 idempotency_conflict; keys are scoped per org and endpoint; a replay adds no
audit row. Use services.idempotency.run_once.

inputs.ticket_text:
Issue edits need optimistic concurrency. The If-Match rule is the same for all three issue
write endpoints, and app/api/middleware.py already sees every request.

GET /issues/{issue_id} returns ETag: "<version>". PATCH /issues/{issue_id}, POST
/issues/{issue_id}/assign, and POST /issues/{issue_id}/transition accept an optional If-Match:
"<version>": without it the write works as before; a stale or malformed one gives 412
precondition_failed; every success increments version and returns the new ETag. Check order: 401,
403 (role), 404 (org, deleted), 412, 422. The 412 status is in the OpenAPI schema.
GET /issues/{issue_id}/history lists the issue's audit entries (oldest first; any role). Board: the
edit form sends the version in a hidden version field; a stale save returns HTTP 409 with a message
page.
